body: {"items":[{"id":"2026-21387","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21387/airworthiness-directives-airbus-helicopters","summary":"The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus Helicopters Model AS350B3, AS355F, AS355F1, AS355F2, AS355N, AS355NP, EC130B4, and EC130T2 helicopters. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of the loss of the tightening torque between the upper ball bearing end and a main rotor (MR) servo-control. This proposed AD would require an inspection of the nut tightening torque of the upper ball bearing end of all the MR servo-controls and, depending on the results, corrective actions. The proposed AD would also require reporting the inspection results. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21334","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21334/airworthiness-directives-airbus-sas-airplanes","summary":"The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2025-09-07, which applies to certain Airbus SAS Model A330-243, -243F, -841, and -941 airplanes. AD 2025-09-07 requires revising the existing airplane flight manual (AFM) by providing instructions to address dual loss of radio management panel (RMP) data synchronization, and the existing minimum equipment list (MEL) by removing relief for an inoperative RMP 3. Since the FAA issued AD 2025-09-07, a modification that addresses the unsafe condition has been developed. This proposed AD would continue to require the actions specified in AD 2025-09-07 and would require modifying the airplane. This proposed AD also reduces the applicability. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts under certain conditions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21333","title":"Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21333/airworthiness-directives-the-boeing-company-airplanes","summary":"The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 737-600, -700, -700C, -800, -900, and -900ER series airplanes. This AD was prompted by reports from multiple operators of pitch oscillation events due to excessive horizontal stabilizer freeplay. This AD requires measuring the freeplay of the horizontal stabilizer pivot hinges and the jackscrew and applicable on- condition actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21332","title":"Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21332/airworthiness-directives-the-boeing-company-airplanes","summary":"The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 737-600, -700, -700C, -800, -900, and -900ER series airplanes. This AD was prompted by a report that some passenger service unit (PSU)-mounted video monitors became detached from the PSU rails during a hard landing. This AD requires replacing PSU-mounted video monitors that do not have secondary retention lanyards. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21331","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21331/airworthiness-directives-airbus-sas-airplanes","summary":"The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2025-04- 05, which applied to all Airbus SAS Model A330-841 and -941 airplanes. AD 2025-04-05 required a revision of the existing airplane flight manual (AFM) and removal of the previously required limitations; a revision of the existing minimum equipment list (MEL); one-time or repetitive seal integrity tests of each engine bleed air system (EBAS) high pressure valve (HPV); additional maintenance instructions and corrective actions; and repetitive replacement of affected HPV clips; as applicable. AD 2025-04-05 also limited the installation of affected HPV clips. Since the FAA issued AD 2025-04-05, an improved EBAS HPV with unaffected HPV clips was certified, and it was determined that the bleed monitoring computer (BMC) software (SW) must be updated. This AD continues to require the actions in AD 2025-04-05, except for repetitive replacement of affected HPV clips. This AD also requires updating the BMC SW, additional work, and an additional revision of the existing MEL for the engine bleed overpressure valve; as applicable. This AD also prohibits the installation of certain BMC software. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21326","title":"Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21326/airworthiness-directives-the-boeing-company-airplanes","summary":"The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 787-8, 787-9, and 787-10 airplanes. This AD was prompted by a report indicating that the protection system on the left fan cowl of the right engine does not sufficiently cover the components and systems from possible cross engine debris. This AD requires performing a maintenance records check or inspection of the right engine to determine the part number of the left fan cowl and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21325","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21325/airworthiness-directives-airbus-sas-airplanes","summary":"The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus SAS Model A330-243, A330-243F, A330-341, A330-342, A330-343, A330-841, and A330-941 airplanes; and Model A340-211, A340-212, A340- 213, A340-311, A340-312, A340-313, A340-541, and A340-642 airplanes. This AD was prompted by reports of leaks on closed fuel low pressure shut-off valves (LPSOVs). This AD requires repetitive leak checks of certain fuel LPSOVs and replacement of an affected part if any discrepancy is detected. This AD also allows the installation of an affected part under certain conditions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21308","title":"Hazardous Materials: Notice of Actions on Special Permits","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21308/hazardous-materials-notice-of-actions-on-special-permits","summary":"In accordance with the procedures governing the application for, and the processing of, special permits from the Department of Transportation's Hazardous Material Regulations, notice is hereby given that the Office of Hazardous Materials Safety has granted or denied the application described herein.","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21307","title":"Hazardous Materials: Notice of Applications for Modification to Special Permits","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21307/hazardous-materials-notice-of-applications-for-modification-to-special-permits","summary":"In accordance with the procedures governing the application for, and the processing of, special permits from the Department of Transportation's Hazardous Material Regulations, notice is hereby given that the Office of Hazardous Materials Safety has received the application described herein.","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21306","title":"Hazardous Materials: Notice of Applications for New Special Permits","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21306/hazardous-materials-notice-of-applications-for-new-special-permits","summary":"In accordance with the procedures governing the application for, and the processing of, special permits from the Department of Transportation's Hazardous Material Regulations, notice is hereby given that the Office of Hazardous Materials Safety has received the application described herein.","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21298","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Pratt & Whitney RTX Corporation (Type Certificate Previously Held by Pratt & Whitney Division United Technologies Corporation) Engines","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21298/airworthiness-directives-pratt-and-whitney-rtx-corporation-type-certificate-previously-held-by-pratt","summary":"The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2026-09-02, which applies to certain Pratt & Whitney RTX Corporation (PW) Model PW4074, PW4074D, PW4077, PW4077D, PW4084D, PW4090, and PW4090-3 engines. AD 2026-09-02 requires repetitive angle ultrasonic scan inspections (AUSIs) of the high-pressure compressor (HPC) 15th- stage disks, front turbine hubs, high-pressure turbine (HPT) 1st-stage air seals, and HPT 2nd-stage hubs for crack indications, and removal from service and replacement if necessary, and for certain serial numbers, removal from service and replacement of the HPT 1st-stage air seal. Since the FAA issued AD 2026-09-02, the FAA was notified that a certain part number was omitted from AD 2026-09-02 and the applicability of the optional terminating action was matched to an unrelated requirement. This proposed AD would require repetitive AUSIs of the HPC 15th-stage disks, front turbine hubs, HPT 1st-stage air seals, and HPT 2nd-stage hubs for crack indications, and removal from service and replacement if necessary, and for certain serial numbers, removal from service and replacement of the HPT 1st-stage air seal. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21290","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Pratt & Whitney Division Engines","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21290/airworthiness-directives-pratt-and-whitney-division-engines","summary":"The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Pratt & Whitney Division (PW) Model PW4052, PW4056, PW4060, PW4060A, PW4060C, PW4062, PW4062A, PW4152, PW4156, PW4156A, PW4158, PW4460, and PW4462 engines. This AD was prompted by multiple reports of tailpipe fire, loss of thrust control, and engine in-flight shutdown due to undetected deterioration of pressure burner (Pb) sensors. This AD requires replacing Pb sensors. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21278","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Rolls-Royce Deutschland Ltd & Co KG Engines","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21278/airworthiness-directives-rolls-royce-deutschland-ltd-and-co-kg-engines","summary":"The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2009-04-13 for certain Rolls-Royce Deutschland Ltd & Co KG (RRD) Model BR700- 715A1-30, BR700-715B1-30, and BR700-715C1-30 engines. AD 2009-04-13 required revising the airworthiness limitations section (ALS) of the operator's existing approved engine maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive tasks and limitations and associated thresholds and intervals for life-limited parts. AD 2009-04-13 also required removing certain low-pressure compressor (LPC) (fan) disc assemblies from service and completing the Life Limited Part Tracking Sheet. Since the FAA issued AD 2009-04-13, the manufacturer has revised the engine time limits manual (TLM) to introduce new or more restrictive tasks and limitations and associated thresholds and intervals for life-limited parts. This AD requires revising the ALS of the existing approved engine maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive tasks and limitations and associated thresholds and intervals for life-limited parts. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21273","title":"DOT Advisory Committee on Human Trafficking","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21273/dot-advisory-committee-on-human-trafficking","summary":"The Office of the Secretary of Transportation (OST) announces the DOT Advisory Committee on Human Trafficking's public meetings in 2026 and 2027. This notice announces the dates, times, and locations of the virtual meetings, which will be open to the public. The purpose of the ACHT is to advise the Secretary of Transportation on countering human trafficking in the transportation sector.","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21264","title":"Agency Information Collection Activities; Submission to the Office of Management and Budget for Review and Approval; Request for Comment; Older Novice Driver Study","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21264/agency-information-collection-activities-submission-to-the-office-of-management-and-budget-for","summary":"In compliance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA), this notice announces that the Information Collection Request (ICR) summarized below will be submitted to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and approval. The ICR describes the nature of the information collection and its expected burden. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) proposes to conduct a new information collection, Older Novice Driver Study. This study aims to examine the driving performance and behavior of younger (less than age 17) and older (ages 18 to 20) novice drivers during their first year of unsupervised driving to inform the feasibility of developing Graduated Driver Licensing (GDL) provisions that apply to older novice drivers. This study will also examine the driving performance and behavior of novices who are consistently at higher- or lower-risk during this period to inform the development of other behavioral countermeasures like training, education, and messaging. A Federal Register Notice with a 60-day comment period soliciting comments on the following information collection was published on May 26, 2026. NHTSA did not receive any comments on the proposed information collection.","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21237","title":"Agency Information Collection Activities: Request for Comments for a New Information Collection","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/19/2026-21237/agency-information-collection-activities-request-for-comments-for-a-new-information-collection","summary":"The FHWA invites public comments about our intention to request the Office of Management and Budget's (OMB) approval for a new information collection, which is summarized below under Supplementary Information. We are required to publish this notice in the Federal Register by the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995.","publishedAt":"2026-10-19","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21228","title":"Agency Information Collection Activities: Request for Comments for a New Information Collection","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/16/2026-21228/agency-information-collection-activities-request-for-comments-for-a-new-information-collection","summary":"The FHWA has forwarded the information collection request described in this notice to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to approve a new information collection. We are required to publish this notice in the Federal Register by the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995.","publishedAt":"2026-10-16","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21192","title":"Establishment of United States Area Navigation Route T-550 and Revocation of Very High Frequency Omnidirectional Range Federal Airway V-320","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/16/2026-21192/establishment-of-united-states-area-navigation-route-t-550-and-revocation-of-very-high-frequency","summary":"This action revokes Very High Frequency (VHF) Omnidirectional Range (VOR) Federal Airway V-320 in Alaska due to navigational signal limits causing portions of this route to be unusable. There are two routes with the identifier V-320, one located in the state of Alaska, and one located in the state of Michigan. This action only revokes the V-320 located in Alaska. FAA is also establishing United States Area Navigation (RNAV) Route T-550 near Anchorage, AK.","publishedAt":"2026-10-16","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21181","title":"Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority's Request To Amend Its Positive Train Control System","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/16/2026-21181/massachusetts-bay-transportation-authoritys-request-to-amend-its-positive-train-control-system","summary":"This document provides the public with notice that, on September 24, 2026, the Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority (MBTA) submitted a request for amendment (RFA) to its FRA-certified positive train control (PTC) system to install Construction Zone (CZ) Transponders on its Worcester Main Line (WML) segment during December 2026. The installation of the CZ is required to reconfigure PTC on the WML between Control Point (CP) 11 (BL 11.40) and CP-21 (BL 21.30). The CZ will result in the suspension of portions of MBTA's PTC system on the WML. As this RFA involves a request for FRA's approval of proposed material modifications to an FRA-certified PTC system, FRA is publishing this notice and inviting public comment on MBTA's RFA to its PTC system.","publishedAt":"2026-10-16","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21179","title":"Establishment of Restricted Areas R-5306G and R-5306H and Amendment of Restricted Areas R-5306C and R-5306E; Cherry Point, NC","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/16/2026-21179/establishment-of-restricted-areas-r-5306g-and-r-5306h-and-amendment-of-restricted-areas-r-5306c-and","summary":"This action establishes restricted areas R-5306G and R-5306H at Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS), Cherry Point, NC. This action also amends R-5306C and R-5306D by modifying two latitude/longitude coordinates and amends the controlling agency for R-5306A, R-5306C, R- 5306D, and R-5306E to reflect MCAS Cherry Point Combined Center Radar Approach Control (CERAP).","publishedAt":"2026-10-16","source":"Federal Register"}]}
